Judgment

This petition is filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- from respondents on account of damages to petitioner's Santro Car, bearing No.KA-05-MK-3989 in Road Traffic Accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are that, on 18- 08-2021 at about 3.30 p.m., on Mysore road, near RR Nagar Arch, Bengaluru city, driver of Santro Car, bearing No.KA-05-MK-3989 was driven the same slowly, carefully by observing all traffic rules and regulations, at that time driver of bus,
bearing No.NL-01-B-2070 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without observing any traffic rules and regulations dashed against petitioner's Santro Car.
Due to the impact, Santro car was fully damaged.
Immediately after the accident, car was shifted to Lotus Motors, Mysore road, Bengaluru, wherein he got repaired the same by spending Rs.3,50,000/-.
Therefore, petitioner prayed for compensation.
Respondent No.1 remained absent and therefore, it was placed exparte.

3(a). Respondent No.2 admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of bus, bearing No.NL-01-B- 2070 and its validity as on the date of accident, denied the other petition averments generally and contended that the driver of insured vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence at the time of alleged accident, vehicle had no valid registration certificate, permit and fitness certificate, the amount of compensation claimed is highly exorbitant and without any basis.

Further,
it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1 under Section 170 of the M.V.
Act.
For the above denials and contentions it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

4. Based on the pleadings the following issues came to be framed:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that his Santro Car, bearing No.KA05MK3989 damaged in the Road Traffic Accident alleged to have occurred on 18082021 at about 3.30 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Bus, bearing registration No.NL01B2070?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom?

5. Petitioner got himself examined as PW1, examined PW2 and marked 18 documents.
Respondent No.2 did not lead its evidence.
Respondent No.1 is exparte.
6. No arguments by petitioner and respondent No.2.

Perused the pleadings and evidences, on the basis, findings on the issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following REASONS ISSUE No.1:
7.
Petitioner led his oral as well as documentary evidence.
Respondent No.1 remained exparte.
Respondent No.2 didn't lead evidence.
This is a summary proceedings, so, the sum and substance of the pleadings and evidences are only emphasized.
The petitioners need to prove this issue on preponderance of probability as test for proof is preponderance of probability herein.
The petition averments as well as the objections are summarized here in above in the brief facts of the case and objections so these are not repeated here in avoidance of the repetition.
The incident, involvement of vehicle and of issuance of 5 (SCCH-16) MVC 5388/2021 insurance policy and its validity are not in dispute; the negligence and damages are in dispute.

8. Regarding the negligence and damages the petitioner relied on police records viz. True copy of FIR with complaint, IMV report, spot Mahazar, Sketch, notice issued under Sec 133 of MV Act and reply on such notice, charge sheet and repair bill which are marked in - Ex.P1 to P4, Ex.P7 to P10.
As per the final report/charge sheet, filed by Byatarayanapura Traffic Police, the negligence was by the driver of Private Bus bearing No.NL-01-B-2070.
The Spot Mahazar and Sketch depict the scene of occurrence.
The IMV report shows there was no mechanical defect in the vehicles.
As already noted the negligence was by the driver of bus bearing No.NL-01- B-2070 as per the final report.
There was no mechanical defect in the vehicles in the sense the incident could have been occurred due to the negligence only.
Now whose negligence was there is to be seen.
No eyewitness is examined therein.

No contrary evidence by respondent No.2 and nothing is elicited in cross examination of PW1 regarding respondent No.2's version hence,

So that, the police records are considered.
10. Regarding prayer of respondent No.2 about the giving of permission under Section 170 of MV Act does not arise as the petition reached its finality.

11. It is therefore, for the foregoing reasons, it is established that, petitioner's car, bearing No.KA-05-MK- 3989 damaged in the Road Traffic Accident occurred on 7 (SCCH-16) MVC 5388/2021 18-08-2021 at about 3.30 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of bus,
bearing Registration No.NL-01-B-2070 on preponderance of probability.
Hence, this issue is answered affirmatively.

ISSUE No.2:
12.
Ex. P10
and Ex
. P16 are one and the same, according to which total repair cost of the car was Rs.2,28,129/-.
It is also admitted by petitioner in his cross examination on the suggestion put by the learned counsel for Respondent No.2.
Here is no contrary evidence by Respondent No.2 in support of its version.
Ex.P10 and Ex.P16 are considerable, hence those are considered.
As it is found the negligence was by the offended bus the petitioner is entitled to the repair charges incurred on the damages of his car, but not fully as sought for.
Hence, this issue is answered partly in affirmative.
13. In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,28,129/-, which can be rounded off to Rs.2,28,200/-.

Keeping in view the interest on the savings by the nationalized banks and as provided under Section 34 of the CPC, in the present case, from the date of petition only the interest at 6% per annum is considered to be directed till its realization.

So, the petitioner is entitled to the interest at 6% per annum on the compensation amount.
8 (SCCH-16) MVC 5388/2021 Liability:
14.
Insurance policy and its validity are admitted and no breaches are established by the insurer.
As found on the discussions on issue No.1, the negligence was on the part of the driver of the offended bus.
On vicarious liability respondent No.1 being the owner is responsible, respondent No.2 being the insurer of respondent No.1 contractually liable to pay compensation.
Thus, respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
However, initially respondent No.2 is liable to pay the determined compensation.
The petitioner is only entitled to such compensation and not fully as claimed for.
Accordingly, this issue stands answered partly in the affirmative.

sentences.text: In view of the findings on issue No.1 and 2, the petition deserves to be allowed in part.
Hence, the following order is passed:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.2,28,200/- (Rupees two lakhs,
twenty eight thousand and two hundred only) with interest at the 9 (SCCH-16) MVC 5388/2021 rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 -Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released to the petitioner through E- payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
